title: Ulm backend for BundleTrajectory
body:
Make BundleTrajectory use ASE Ulm files instead of Python pickle files.  It can still read the old format.

This solves problems with pickle format not being readable across Python versions.
author: schiotz

comments.author: jensj
comments.body:
Would it be possible to create a new folder+ulm back-end that could be used together with the normal trajectory object?  In the long run, it would be really great if we could have just one trajectory class with several back-ends instead of several trajectory classes.  And since you are anyway switching from bundle+pickle to bundle+ulm, now could be a good time to try that.

The Trajectory class is also missing some much asked for functionality that ``BundleTrajectory`` has (writing extra stuff).  Would be nice if we could have that code in one place.

Anyway, I can merge this if you think it's a bad idea or a too long-term solution.
comments.label_reasoning: The comment suggests restructuring the codebase to consolidate multiple trajectory classes into one class with multiple backends, addressing code organization and module boundaries rather than a specific bug or style issue.

review_threads.actionability_reasoning: The comment suggests a concrete architectural improvement: creating a new folder and ULM back-end that could be shared with the normal trajectory object, unifying multiple trajectory classes into one with several back-ends. It also flags missing functionality that should be consolidated. Even though it ends with an offer to merge as-is, the suggestions imply concrete code changes.

comments.author: schiotz
comments.body: @jensj I just sneaked in a small improvement since it had not been merged yet :-)

comments.author: schiotz
comments.body:
@jensj That is probably possible, I will however have to think about how that should work.  

I would appreciate if you could merge the current BundleTrajectory, for two reasons.  First, it will take a while to extend the normal Trajectory in this way.  Second, I am currently using BundleTrajectory for some *very* large simulations, so it would be nice if ASE can handle the files I am generating now.  With a bit of luck, it will later be possible to merge the two formats.
